From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>

Alex / team —

Reviewing ACME's redline. Below are proposed positions and draft language we should offer back. I'm keeping it pragmatic — preserve Redwood's ability to operate while addressing ACME's concerns.

1) Auto-Renew (Section 2.3)
- Position: Keep auto-renew but shorten the notice window to 60 days for enterprise deals; for pilots less than $50k TCV, allow opt-in renewals.
- Draft: "This Agreement shall automatically renew for successive one-year terms unless either party provides written notice of non-renewal at least sixty (60) days prior to the end of the then-current term. Notwithstanding the foregoing, pilot agreements (defined as commitments with total consideration less than $50,000) require affirmative renewal by mutual written agreement."

2) Termination for Convenience (Section 8)
- Position: Offer TfC with a 60-day wind-down and specified refund formula for pre-paid, unused service credits for pilots or self-serve usage. For Dedicated/Reserved capacity contracts, TfC may incur a termination fee to cover committed infrastructure costs.
- Draft: "Either party may terminate this Agreement for convenience upon sixty (60) days' prior written notice. If Company has prepaid for committed capacity, Redwood will refund a pro rata amount for unused, prepaid service credits, less any reasonable wind-down costs reasonably incurred to transition services. For Dedicated capacity engagements, a termination fee reflecting the unamortized committed infrastructure costs may apply and will be specified in the applicable Order Form."

3) Material Change / Notice Windows
- Position: 45 days is reasonable for major product or pricing changes; define "Material Change" narrowly.

4) Process / Runbook
- Suggest a short mutual action plan: legal redline exchange -> internal legal approval -> procurement confirmation -> finalize redline -> DocuSign. Recommend we own the initial counter within 48 hours after call.

I also flagged a few other small items in the attached doc but these are the major commercial levers. If Alex can confirm ACME's priority (pilot vs reserved capacity) that will determine whether we accept opt-in for renewals or require auto-renew.

-Kim
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Commercial
Redwood Inference

Vivian —

Thanks for your patience while we reviewed ACME's redlines. Per Kim's suggestions above, Redwood is prepared to propose the following compromise: 

- Auto-renew: Auto-renew remains in the MSA with a 60-day cancellation notice for enterprise deals; pilots under $50k will require mutual renewal.
- Notice for Material Changes: We agree to a 45-day notice for specified "Material Changes" with a narrow definition included in Exhibit A.
- Termination for Convenience: 60-day wind-down; pro rata refund for unused prepaid credits for pilots/self-serve; termination fee for dedicated/reserved capacity as specified in the Order Form.

I've attached our marked counter with the exact redline for the MSA (ACME_MSA_redlines_v2.docx) reflecting this language. Next steps: please confirm ACME's engagement type (pilot vs reserved) and whether procurement prefers a DocuSign route or a tracked redline exchange. If it's helpful, let's schedule 30 minutes tomorrow (Thu) 10:00-10:30 PT to finalize — I can send a calendar invite.
